title: Old and new implementations coexist without a cutover plan
task: Review a rewrite program where a new implementation has been added beside the old one, but users can choose either indefinitely.
context: Bug fixes must often be applied twice.
Documentation does not state which implementation new users should adopt.
No removal criteria or migration deadline exists.
evidence: Support issues show user confusion about which implementation is preferred.
The compatibility matrix and CI time have grown because both paths remain active.
Several fixes have already diverged between the two implementations.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Keep both forever because choice is always good.
Continue the rewrite without defining migration or deprecation.
expected_decision_properties: Identify coexistence itself as an engineering cost.
Require a clear supported choice, migration direction, deprecation/removal condition, and ownership plan.
Avoid deleting the old path immediately unless consumer migration evidence makes that safe.
Treat duplicate fixes/test matrix/support burden as part of rewrite economics.
unacceptable_reasoning: Users can decide the architecture strategy for themselves indefinitely.
Rewrite completion is only a code-completeness question.
verification_expectations: Inventory remaining consumers of the old implementation.
Define and test the migration/cutover path.
Track removal criteria and ensure temporary compatibility code has an owner.
